text:
marta: Heads-up — noticed a EU tail-latency spike 03:14-03:22 UTC, autoscaler did not scale up early due to hysteresis + long cooldown. GPUs hit ~92% for ~10m.
linus: same. k8s events show scale decision skipped: reason="hysteresis_active", last_scale=02:50 UTC. logs attached in thread.
marta: @raj can you check if this maps to any traffic forecast or external trigger?
raj: quick glance shows a ~35% uplift in gen QPS starting 02:50 UTC coinciding with marketing email send. We had this in weekend plan but not for this timeslot.
kevin: is the current scale-up cooldown still 120s? that's probably too long for sudden marketing-driven bursts. Concern about oscillation if we shorten it.
linus: current config: scaleUp.stabilizationWindowSeconds=120, policy has hysteresis requiring sustained >70% for 3m before scale. I propose a two-tier policy: short aggressive path for very-high-util spikes and the default slower path for gradual growth.
marta: sounds reasonable. can you post the patch/snippet you propose so we can review? also include cost estimate delta.
linus: patch snippet to test in canary EU cluster: 
```
kubectl patch hpa inference-eu -n production -p '{"spec":{"behavior":{"scaleUp":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":45,"policies":[{"type":"Percent","value":50,"periodSeconds":15}]}}}}'
```
linus: this reduces stabilization window to 45s and allows a single larger percent jump under the short-window path.
autoscale-bot: Scale event applied to canary-eu at 03:23 UTC — +8 pods (policy: short-window override). :rocket:
ops-sre: follow-up guardrail suggestion: cap burst at 20% of reserved GPUs and trigger high-priority alert if burst uses >15% for >30m. That prevents burst floods from draining reserved capacity for steady traffic.
raj: for forecasting, we should ingest marketing campaign webhook signals into the demand predictor so spikes like this are pre-annotated. I'll open a ticket and PR for tagging events.
kevin: cost note: short-window can increase transient cost ~3-6% under noisy traffic. I'm OK with a 24h canary and close monitoring.
marta: I'll monitor the EU dashboards and token-level cost. If we see oscillation or cost >7% vs baseline, we roll back. Created follow-up: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1829
linus: also enabling per-route rate limit backpressure for the most bursty endpoints as a lower-cost safety net. config PR: https://git.company/s/repo/pull/241
marta: thanks team. action items: 1) linus apply canary patch now; 2) raj add marketing signal to demand pipeline; 3) ops-sre add alert + quota guardrail; 4) kevin monitor cost delta. Check-in in 1h. :thumbsup:
